toastSaveSettingsFailed: Couldn’t save the settings. Check that the configuration folder is writable: {error}
toastConfigProblems: {count, plural, one {Your config has # problem: see Settings › Advanced} other {Your config has # problems: see Settings › Advanced}}
cliAddedToPath: Added the kero command to your PATH: new terminals have it
openProjectMessage: Choose a folder: its sessions are grouped under its name.
confirmCloseSessionDetail: {process} is still running in it. Closing the session ends it.
confirmCloseProjectDetail: {count, plural, one {This ends its # session, with what runs in it.} other {This ends its # sessions, with what runs in them.}}
confirmClosePaneDetail: {process} is still running in it. Closing the pane ends it.
confirmQuitAllDetail: {count, plural, one {Kero keeps sessions running when it quits. This ends the # session, with what runs in it.} other {Kero keeps sessions running when it quits. This ends all # of them, with what runs in them.}}
restartRunning: {count, plural, one {A program is running in # session} other {Programs are running in # sessions}}
restartStaleDetail: The service that runs your sessions is still Kero {was}, and this is Kero {version}. {running}: restarting ends them, and sessions start again where they were, with their history.
restartServiceDetail: Every pane’s program ends; the shells start again in their folders, under their history.
footerNeedsYou: {count, plural, one {# session needs you} other {# sessions need you}}
footerWorking: {count, plural, one {# session working} other {# sessions working}}
footerDone: {count, plural, one {# session done, unseen} other {# sessions done, unseen}}
footerServiceTip: Sessions run in kerod, in the background: they keep running when you quit kero.
updateRestartTip: Kero was updated: restart the background service to run the new version
updatedDetail: The background service that runs your sessions is from another version. Restart it: your sessions start again where they were, with their history.
emptyDetail: Sessions keep running in the background — quit Kero and come back to everything just as you left it.
paletteRestartServiceDetail: Sessions start again where they were
palettePlaceholder: Go to session or run a command…
svcRunning: Running (pid {pid}) for {duration} · {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}, {panes, plural, one {# pane} other {# panes}}
svcStale: · still an earlier Kero: restart it to update
setSessionsDetail: Sessions keep running in the background when Kero quits; {action} ends them.
setSessionNameDetail: Until you or an agent name one. With Pane You’re In, a pane running only its shell defers to the pane that needs you most.
setAskBeforeClosing: Ask before closing a running program
setAskBeforeClosingDetail: When a pane or session you close has a program other than the shell running.
setRestoreSessionsDetail: If the background service stops, as when the Mac restarts, sessions start again in their folders, under their history.
setResumeAgentsDetail: Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode pick up their conversation where it was, once Kero’s skill is set up for them in Agents.
setAutoCheckDetail: Once a day, while Kero is open.
setAutoInstallDetail: They take effect the next time Kero opens.
setTranslucentDetail: Let the desktop show through the window’s background.
setGrainDetail: A faint speckle over the background, so flat colors read as material.
setAmbientColorDetail: Let the colour of the album that plays tint the accent, the panes and the terminals' cursor and selection.
setFontDetail: JetBrains Mono with Nerd Fonts’ icons comes with Kero. Any installed monospaced font works; names separated by commas are tried in order.
setLigaturesDetail: Join characters as the font draws them, as => and !=.
setThickenDetail: A heavier stroke, as Ghostty’s font-thicken.
setColorsDetail: Ghostty’s themes, and your own in ~/.config/ghostty/themes.
setOptionMetaDetail: Option sends Alt to programs, as for Emacs and readline, instead of typing accents.
setCopyOnSelectDetail: What you select goes to the clipboard.
setClipboardReadDetail: As with OSC 52: agents asking for what you copied.
setShellGroupDetail: Changes apply to panes started after them.
setScrollbackDetail: How much output each pane keeps, also while no window shows it.
setEnvironmentDetail: Added to every pane’s, over what kero sets (TERM, KERO_SESSION…).
setNotifyUnpackaged: This build can’t post notifications: macOS shows those of packaged apps only.
setNotifyWaitingDetail: A program asks something, rings the bell, or reports it is blocked.
setNotifyDoneDetail: While you look at another session, or another app.
setNotifyThrottleDetail: A session that needs you or ends unseen tells once. A loop of the same session and state inside this window is counted, not announced.
setDockBadgeDetail: With the number of sessions that need you.
setDockBounceDetail: Once, when a session comes to need you.
setRemoteControlDetail: kero do and kero focus run the app’s actions, as its menus do: splitting, switching sessions, opening the palette.
setCliDetail: Inside Kero, every pane has the kero command on its PATH already.
setCliNotInstalled: Not installed: other terminals don’t know the kero command.
setSkillsDetail: Teaches agents to start sessions and panes, drive them, wait for them and report their status, and tells them, as they start, which session they’re in.
setProgramStatusDetail: Programs report what they do with OSC 7501, Superlogical’s program status protocol: the sidebar shows it, and notifies you.
setConfigurationDetail: Every setting here is a line of this file, as Ghostty’s: edit it in any editor, and what you save applies at once. kero config show lists every key.
setBackgroundServiceDetail: kerod runs your sessions: quitting kero leaves it running.
setResetDetail: Back to how Kero comes, shortcuts included.
setKeyboardHelp: Click a shortcut, then type the new one. Delete removes it; Escape keeps it.
setShortcutNeedsMac: A shortcut needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it is a function key.
setShortcutNeedsPc: A shortcut needs Ctrl or Alt, unless it is a function key.
linearGroupDetail: The workspace's issues, in a board or a list, with the session working on one beside them.
linearStatusAuthFailed: Linear refused the API key. Set a new one in Settings › Linear.
linearStatusRateLimited: Linear is rate limiting the reads; the next one is later.
linearStatusUnreachable: Linear could not be reached. Check the connection; the last read stays.
linearStatusDisabled: Linear is turned off. Turn it on in Settings › Linear.
linearNoneDetail: Linear has no issues to show here.
linearNotReadDetail: Set a Linear API key in Settings › Linear, and the workspace will load.
linearUnavailableDetail: Could not read the issue. Check the connection and retry.
linearNoSession: No session is working on this issue.
setLinearRefreshDetail: How often the service asks Linear what changed. Linear allows a key 2,500 requests an hour.
paneTerminalDetail: A shell in the session's folder
paneFilesDetail: Browse and read the project's files
paneBrowserDetail: A web page, such as your dev server
panePluginDetail: A widget of a plugin, such as Spotify
pluginTreePlaceholder: This plugin's interface is on its way
pluginPinSettingDetail: A row above the sessions that opens the plugin beside your terminals.
pluginUnknownDetail: No plugin {id} is installed. Install it, then open a pane of it.
pluginStartingDetail: The plugin starts when its first pane opens.
pluginNeedsRestart: Plugin panes need a newer terminal service. Restart the terminal service, then try again.
pluginSettingsGroupDetail: Plugins add panes of their own. Their settings and secrets are kept in the data folder, apart from their code.
pluginNoneDetail: Built-in plugins come with the app. Installed plugins live in the configuration folder's plugins folder.
pluginCommandNoSession: Open a session first: a {name} command runs in a pane of it.
spotifyNotRunningDetail: The pane plays what Spotify plays. Open Spotify, then come back.
spotifyNotInstalledDetail: The pane plays what the Spotify app plays. Install Spotify for Mac, then come back.
spotifyAutomationDetail: Allow Shibu Code to control Spotify in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Automation, then reopen this pane.
spotifyUnavailableDetail: The pane could not read the player. Try again in a moment.
spotifyPlayHereDetail: Sign in with your Spotify Premium account. Music plays in Shibu Code, with no Spotify app open.
spotifyStreamAgainTitle: Sign in again to play here
spotifyStreamAgainDetail: Your sign-in is from before Shibu Code could play music itself. Sign in once more to play here.
spotifyPremiumRequiredNotice: Spotify Premium is needed to play here.
spotifySignInAgainNotice: Sign in to Spotify again to play here.
spotifyNoClientIDDetail: Create an app in the Spotify developer dashboard with {uri} as its redirect URI, paste its Client ID in Settings › Plugins, then sign in here.
spotifySignedOut: Sign in to browse your library
spotifySignedOutDetail: Playback controls work without signing in. Sign in to search albums and playlists.
spotifyTokenRefusedDetail: Sign in again to browse your playlists and albums.
spotifyPremiumDetail: Spotify only lets this kind of app search its catalog with a Premium account.
spotifyRateLimited: Spotify asked to wait, showing the last results
spotifyRateLimitedDetail: Too many requests in a short time. Try again in a minute.
spotifySearchPromptDetail: Find an album or a playlist, then play it from here.
spotifyNoPlaylistsDetail: Save a playlist in Spotify, then it shows here.
spotifyNoAlbumsDetail: Save an album in Spotify, then it shows here.
spotifySignInFailed: Could not sign in to Spotify.
spotifyLibraryFailed: Spotify could not load your library.
spotifyTracksForbidden: Spotify doesn't share this playlist's tracks
spotifyTracksScope: Sign in again to let Shibu Code read collaborative playlists.
spotifyNoTracksDetail: There is nothing to play here.
spotifyQueueEmptyDetail: Tracks that come next show here.
paneAttentionDetail: Every session that needs you, in one list
attentionEmptyDetail: Sessions that work, wait on you or end unseen show here, with the pane to open.
attentionEmptyFilteredDetail: Another filter, or no search, may show what you look for.
paneNoRoom: Not enough room for another pane here
browserCantOpen: Check the address and try again
browserNoServers: No servers are listening right now.
browserHint: Type an address, a port such as 3000, or words to search for.
filesCantRead: Can’t read this. Check that it still exists and that you may open it.
confirmShowDetail: {process} is still running in it, and ends when the pane shows something else.
tasksLinkDetail: The pane shows that project's issues, and agents in this project start their work from them.
tasksShowAll: Show the whole team’s issues instead
usagePluginHelpClaude: Reads your Claude Code sign-in. Run claude and sign in, then refresh.
usagePluginHelpCodex: Reads your Codex sign-in, or OpenCode’s OpenAI login. Run codex login, then refresh.
usagePluginHelpOpencode: Reads your OpenCode workspace key. If it expired, sign in through OpenCode or enter a replacement key in the Usage tab.
usagePluginHelpDeepseek: Direct DeepSeek API credit. For DeepSeek through OpenCode Go, use the OpenCode allowance instead.
linearNotShown: {count} more issues are not shown. Narrow them with a filter or fold a section.
linearServiceDown: The Shibu service is not reachable
linearLinkInProjectMenu: Link it in the project's menu, or show every issue for now.
sessionOrderUnavailable: Reconnect to the terminal service before reordering sessions.
sessionOrderMissing: Session not found. Choose a current session and try again.
setSourceUpdatesDetail: Check Kero upstream and build Shibu in GitHub. Requires gh signed in as ddeyalla.
projectOrderMissing: Project not found. Choose a current project and try again.
